definition: Paul Christiano is an American researcher in the field of artificial intelligence (AI), with a specific focus on AI alignment, which is the subfield of AI safety research that aims to steer AI systems toward human interests.
details: He is the founder and executive director of the Alignment Research Center (ARC), a nonprofit that develops methods for finding mechanistic explanations of neural network behavior, and serves on the Safety and Security Committee of the OpenAI Foundation's board. Christiano worked at OpenAI from 2017 to 2021, where he led the language model alignment team and became one of the principal architects of reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF). He founded ARC in 2021 and in 2024 became Head of Safety for the U.S. AI Safety Institute (now the Center for AI Standards and Innovation) inside NIST, before returning to ARC as executive director. He was also an initial trustee of Anthropic's Long-Term Benefit Trust. In 2023, Christiano was named to the TIME 100 Most Influential People in AI and appointed to the advisory board of the UK government's Frontier AI Taskforce.

explainer.lead: Paul Christiano is an American AI safety researcher. His work spans artificial intelligence and AI alignment.

contributions.name: While at Berkeley, Christiano collaborated with researcher Katja Grace on AI Impacts, co-developing a preliminary methodology for comparing supercomputers to brains, using traversed edges per second (TEPS).
At OpenAI, Christiano co-authored the paper "Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences" (2017) and other works developing reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
Christiano left OpenAI in 2021 to work on more conceptual and theoretical issues in AI alignment and subsequently founded the Alignment Research Center to focus on this area.
In April 2023, Christiano told The Economist that ARC was considering developing an industry standard for AI safety.

timeline.what: He competed on the U.S. team and won a silver medal at the 49th International Mathematics Olympiad (IMO) in 2008.
In 2012, Christiano graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) with a degree in mathematics.
Doctor of Philosophy, University of California, Berkeley
He completed a PhD at the University of California, Berkeley in 2017.
He is considered one of the principal architects of RLHF, which in 2017 was "considered a notable step forward in AI safety research", according to The New York Times.

In March 2024, VentureBeat reported, citing at least two anonymous sources, that staff members and scientists at NIST threatened to resign over Christiano's expected appointment, citing concerns that his ties to the effective altruism movement could jeopardize the AI Safety Institute's objectivity and integrity.
